text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Spike detected - API Gateway 5xx rate increased from 0.4% to 18% in the last 5m. Primary error codes: 502, 504. Affected route(s): /v1/generate, /v1/stream. Link: https://metrics.internal.redwood/alerts/1769901123

alex (oncall): looking. paging SRE oncall @maya and API owners @riley

maya (sre): I can take. can someone drop the top-level error graph and the gateway logs?

riley (api-gateway): seeing a sharp rise in 502s at the edge. Logs show upstream timeouts to runtime pool nodes. snippet below:
```
[2026-03-14T09:02:14Z] gateway: upstream="10.0.34.12:8080" status=502 condition="upstream_read_timeout" route="/v1/generate"
[2026-03-14T09:02:15Z] gateway: upstream="10.0.34.15:8080" status=504 condition="connection_reset" route="/v1/stream"
[2026-03-14T09:02:16Z] gateway: upstream="10.0.34.12:8080" status=502 condition="upstream_write_timeout"
```

riley (api-gateway): envoy stats: cluster.runtime_pool.upstream_rq_5xx = +1700 in 5m. latency p95 on gateway up to 900ms.

sam (network): I don't see LB config changes in the last 24h. health checks to runtime instances are OK but some nodes flapping Unhealthy->Healthy. digging into cloud LB logs now.

deploy-bot: deploy event: service=runtime-pool tag=release-2026-03-14-08:59 initiated by pipeline #deploy-8912 at 2026-03-14T08:59:03Z

alex (oncall): possible correlation with that rollout. maya, can you confirm whether the runtime pool has any recent config or JVM/GC changes?

maya (sre): looking. no JVM flags changed but the release bumped tokenization lib and switched a default of streaming chunking size. runtime pods log show increased GC pauses on a subset of pods. sample:
```
[2026-03-14T08:58:34Z] runtime: GC pause 320ms heapBefore=1.9G heapAfter=1.7G
[2026-03-14T08:59:01Z] runtime: request=abcdef duration=1200ms status=504
```

maya (sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback runtime release 2) scale runtime pool and gate high-latency callers behind rate-limits at gateway 3) enable proxy-level circuit breaker to return 429/503 for overloaded downstream vs 502/504.

riley (api-gateway): can we flip temporary route-level rate limit for /v1/generate to 50r/s per api-key? also toggle prefix caching bypass for streaming?

alex (oncall): do it. riley, post commands. I'll coordinate rollback path with deploy team.\
riley (api-gateway): running patch: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gateway-rate-limits-temp
data:
  /v1/generate: "50"
EOF`
Applying now... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

riley (api-gateway): rate-limit config applied. confirming counters: /v1/generate dropped from 1200r/s to 220r/s at gateway edge in 30s. 5xx rate now trending down.

maya (sre): scaling runtime-pool +3 pods: `kubectl scale deployment/runtime-pool --replicas=12` (was 9). also cordoned two suspected pods for deeper investigation.

sam (network): LB logs show 10.0.34.12 had repeated connection resets at 08:59-09:01 cluster network path looks fine, likely app-level. I've quarantined that instance from the target group.

alex (oncall): deploy-bot, can you confirm rollback plan and estimated time for safe rollback?\
deploy-bot: rollback plan: canary rollback prepared. steps: 1) promote previous image (release-2026-03-13-21) to canary 2) monitor error rate for 5m 3) promote to full if stable. Estimated time to canary: 4 minutes.

jess (cs): heads up — CS reporting 3 customers on enterprise tier issued support tickets about intermittent 502s since 09:00. estimated impacted calls ~18% for those orgs. asking for ETA to resolution.

maya (sre): Recommend we do canary rollback to test if release caused regressions. will monitor tokenization errors and GC metrics.

alex (oncall): proceed with canary rollback. riley keep rate-limiting in place until we see consistent drop. sam keep offending node isolated. jess push proactive note to the three customers: short explanation + mitigation steps + ETA 30m.

riley (api-gateway): rate limits remain. 5xx now down to 6% and trending. p95 latency back to 320ms. partial relief.

deploy-bot: canary rollback completed at 1769901542 (2026-03-14T09:12:22Z). monitoring window started.

maya (sre): post-canary metrics: canary cluster error 5xx=0.6% vs current runtime pool 5xx=5.8% (pre-rollback). looks like the release is correlated. recommend full rollback.

alex (oncall): proceed full rollback, coordinate with infra to avoid cascading restarts. jess, you can escalate to account teams.

riley (api-gateway): full rollback in progress. will keep rate-limits for 15 more minutes then re-evaluate.

sam (network): quarantined node reintroduced after restart and passes health checks. no network-level issues found.

jess (cs): sent customer notes to affected accounts: short summary + ETA updated to 15m, asked them to retry - gave a safe fallback pattern.

maya (sre): full rollback completed at 1769901788. observing cluster: 5xx dropped to 0.9% overall. GC pause patterns normalized on previously flapping nodes.

alex (oncall): excellent. summary for handoff: cause = runtime release (tokenization change) triggered GC/backpressure on subset of runtime pods -> upstream timeouts -> gateway 502/504 spike. mitigations performed: temporary gateway route rate-limits, isolate/quarantine bad pods, scale + rollback release. customer impact: transient 5xx spike ~9-18% on some routes for ~20m, 3 enterprise customers reported issues. actions: postmortem, add release gate for tokenization change, add runtime canary step focused on GC/latency, improve alert to surface rollout correlation. link to timeline & logs: https://incidents.redwood/1769901123/timeline

maya (sre): handing off to night oncall @alex (oncall) at 1769902000. next steps: follow up on postmortem, ensure rate-limit removed after 30m, verify no regression in next 2h.

alex (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll monitor next 2h and open a postmortem ticket. :white_check_mark:
